section_summary: These pages trace the adoption and implementation of Far Eastern Commission policy on trade marks, trade names, and merchandise marking in occupied Japan. They also document disputes over similar corporate names, the VOGUE title, Ajinomoto distribution, and a copied British textile design. Correspondence explains how foreign owners could restore registrations and protect their rights.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Proposed U.S. instructions on the FEC trade mark paper.
subfiles.summary: Approve restoration provisions but seek deletion of provisions on SCAP intervention and merchandise marking.

subfiles.title: FEC C1-332, Trade-marks and Marking of Merchandise in Japan
subfiles.about: Routes a draft cable seeking SCAP's views on an amendment.
subfiles.summary: Explains the attached draft cable and Army memorandum.

subfiles.title: Letter on proposed FEC trade mark amendment
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP's view on revised merchandise origin marking language.
subfiles.summary: Reports the committee vote and explains why SCAP's assessment is needed before setting a U.S. position.

subfiles.title: Draft cable to SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks views on the committee's revised marking provision.
subfiles.summary: Quotes the amendment covering marking and advertising of Japanese exports.

subfiles.title: Office of Alien Property concurrence in Japanese trade mark policy
subfiles.about: Confirms interagency approval of the State-Army Japanese trade mark policy.
subfiles.summary: The Office of Alien Property broadly concurs but qualifies its power to prohibit mark use and issue royalty-free licenses. State treats those concerns as procedural or covered by exceptions and asks Army to transmit the policy to SCAP. Page 81 contains a duplicate, degraded version of the closing page, followed by a clearer copy on page 82.

subfiles.title: Trade Marks, C1-332/2
subfiles.about: Assesses the FEC paper's scope and competing marking provisions.
subfiles.summary: Supports broad FEC consideration but advises continued opposition to the revised export marking requirement pending SCAP's views.

subfiles.title: Response on marking provision in trade-marks paper
subfiles.about: Compares the original and amended origin marking language.
subfiles.summary: Finds the amendment more demanding and its advertising restriction difficult to enforce abroad.

subfiles.title: Marking provision in trade-marks paper
subfiles.about: Requests legal assessment of two marking provisions.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether the committee amendment imposes stricter duties on SCAP and Japan.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Sets U.S. instructions for FEC C1-332/2.
subfiles.summary: Directs approval of restoration provisions and seeks deletion of paragraphs 6–8, while allowing separate fair-trade policy consideration.

subfiles.title: Army report on similar Japanese corporate names
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP's investigation of rival corn-products firms' names.
subfiles.summary: Describes Japanese trade-name law, the firms' positions, and a proposed name change. Army asks for Corn Products Refining Company's opinion before the Japanese shareholders meet.

subfiles.title: Interim report of action taken by the Japanese Government
subfiles.about: Reports progress toward changing the disputed company name.
subfiles.summary: The firm plans a May vote and will mark existing materials to disclaim association with Japan Corn Products Refining Company.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Colonel Riggs
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Army's report on the trade-name dispute.
subfiles.summary: Refers the matter to J. N. Lightman while Bishop is away.

subfiles.title: Proposed settlement of similar trade names
subfiles.about: Asks Corn Products Refining Company to assess the proposed name change.
subfiles.summary: Describes the planned new name and temporary disclaimer on existing stationery and containers.

subfiles.title: Corn Products Refining Company's settlement response
subfiles.about: Accepts a proposed name change with conditions.
subfiles.summary: Requests a two-month limit and a disclaimer naming the Japanese subsidiary.

subfiles.title: State report of Corn Products Refining Company's response
subfiles.about: Conveys the American company's conditions for settling the name dispute.
subfiles.summary: Reports acceptance of the change with a limited period for using old materials and a revised disclaimer.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to Colonel Riggs
subfiles.about: Drafts State's report on the proposed trade-name settlement.
subfiles.summary: Relays Corn Products Refining Company's requested time limit and disclaimer wording.

subfiles.title: Request for SCAP's view on FEC marking provision
subfiles.about: Requests a cable asking SCAP about proposed export marking language.
subfiles.summary: Notes strong FEC support and seeks SCAP's assessment before State decides whether to support it.

subfiles.title: Complaint about Japanese use of VOGUE
subfiles.about: Seeks the proper authority for a magazine-title infringement complaint.
subfiles.summary: Counsel for Condé Nast reports a Japanese fashion magazine titled VOGUE and asks whom to contact.

subfiles.title: Reply on VOGUE trade mark complaint
subfiles.about: Explains where to submit details of the alleged infringement.
subfiles.summary: Directs counsel to SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section and the Army Civil Affairs Division.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of VOGUE guidance
subfiles.about: Confirms counsel will pursue the recommended contacts.
subfiles.summary: Plans to send the full case to General Marquat and Colonel Porter.

subfiles.title: Army update on corn-products company name
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese firm's shareholder vote on its name.
subfiles.summary: Shareholders voted to rename the company Nippon Shokuhin Kako Kabushiki Kaisha.

subfiles.title: Notice to Corn Products Refining Company
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese company's vote to change its name.
subfiles.summary: Advises the complainant of the May shareholder decision.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Far Eastern Commission policy decision
subfiles.about: Sends the adopted policy and asks for a directive to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the decision and explanatory table, requesting notice when the directive reaches Tokyo so the policy can be released.

subfiles.title: Certification of adopted FEC document
subfiles.about: Certifies the attached FEC document against its original.
subfiles.summary: Certifies the copy as correct.

subfiles.title: Trade-Marks, Trade Names and Marking of Merchandise in Japan
subfiles.about: Sets occupation policy for trade mark restoration and fair marking.
subfiles.summary: Provides for restoration, reinstatement, priority claims, cancellation of confusing marks, truthful descriptions of Japanese goods, and corresponding protection for trade names.

subfiles.title: Examples of application of second sentence of paragraph 1
subfiles.about: Illustrates restored registration terms with hypothetical dates.
subfiles.summary: Tables six examples of protection periods after restoration.

subfiles.title: Request to transmit FEC trade mark directive
subfiles.about: Asks Army to send the draft directive through the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
subfiles.summary: Explains the FEC decision, requests transmission to General MacArthur, and asks for acknowledgment so the policy can be published.

subfiles.title: Draft directive regarding trade-marks, trade names and marking
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Drafts instructions implementing the FEC policy.
subfiles.summary: Reproduces the nine policy provisions on restoration, applications, confusing marks, merchandise descriptions, and trade names.

subfiles.title: Appendix: examples of restored registration periods
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Supplies hypothetical calculations for restored trade mark terms.
subfiles.summary: Tables six registration, restoration, and expiration scenarios.

subfiles.title: Army transmission of Directive Serial No. 105
subfiles.about: Confirms the directive was cabled to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Encloses four copies and requests notice when the certified copy is filed with the FEC.

subfiles.title: Directive Serial No. 105, copy 2
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Transmits the FEC policy as occupation guidance.
subfiles.summary: Sets out all nine policy provisions for restoring foreign trade mark rights and preventing confusing marks and misleading descriptions of Japanese exports.

subfiles.title: Directive Serial No. 105, copy 3, opening page
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Begins a second copy of the directive.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the directive's heading and opening restoration provision.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Army's directive copies
subfiles.about: Confirms receipt and FEC filing of Directive 105.
subfiles.summary: States that certified copy 1 was sent to the FEC Secretary General.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding certified Directive 105
subfiles.about: Forwards the certified directive for Commission files.
subfiles.summary: Encloses certified copy 1 of Directive 105.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about restoration and renewal dates
subfiles.about: Asks how expired American registrations will be renewed under FEC policy.
subfiles.summary: Seeks deadlines and clarification on preserving original priority while calculating renewed registration terms.

subfiles.title: Reply on restoration and renewal of registrations
subfiles.about: Explains restoration periods and later renewal under Japanese law.
subfiles.summary: Restored rights retain the unexpired term held at the outbreak of hostilities. Owners may then renew, with a fee, while preserving the original priority date.

subfiles.title: Despatch 647 transmitting SCAPIN 2042
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP's implementation memorandum and a press release.
subfiles.summary: Describes restoration, future protection, and bans on misleading marks; promises translations of Japanese implementing measures.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 2042: Trade-Marks, Trade Names and Marking of Merchandise
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs Japan to implement the FEC trade mark policy.
subfiles.summary: Orders restoration and reinstatement, priority claims, cancellation of confusing marks, and accurate merchandise descriptions. Requests must generally be filed within one year of implementing legislation; Japan must submit proposed measures within thirty days.

subfiles.title: Trade-Mark Rights to Be Restored
subfiles.from: Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Announces SCAP's trade mark directive.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes restoration and priority rights, protection against confusing registrations, truthful marking requirements, and the filing period.

subfiles.title: Request for copy of SCAPIN 2042
subfiles.about: Requests the September SCAP trade mark memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Asks State to send SCAPIN 2042 if available.

subfiles.title: Reply to request for SCAPIN 2042
subfiles.about: Explains the directive and promises later implementing regulations.
subfiles.summary: Quotes its opening and closing provisions, notes that FEC policy was previously sent, and offers future Japanese orders.

subfiles.title: Office of Alien Property inquiry on Ajinomoto licenses
subfiles.to: Office of the Undersecretary of the Army, attention Edward W. Hendrick
subfiles.about: Questions an exclusive Ajinomoto export arrangement and its effect on trade mark licenses.
subfiles.summary: The Office had issued revocable, nonexclusive, royalty-free licenses for the Ajinomoto mark. Reports of an exclusive agreement with Wilbur-Ellis raise concern that other licensed importers cannot obtain goods. Baynton requests Army and SCAP views before deciding whether to continue the license.

subfiles.title: Despatch 802 on British textile design complaint
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits correspondence about alleged copying of a British fabric design.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the complaint and SCAP's advice that British firms register designs in Japan.

subfiles.title: Tootal Broadhurst Lee design complaint
subfiles.from: J. M. Luxmoore, Tootal Broadhurst Lee Company
subfiles.to: Board of Trade, attention S. D. Wingate
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese fabric closely imitating a registered British design.
subfiles.summary: Describes samples found in Singapore and asks whether occupation authorities can stop copying or identify the importer.

subfiles.title: Board of Trade referral of design complaint
subfiles.about: Asks the U.K. mission to raise the fabric-copying complaint with SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Notes that registration in Japan offers a remedy but requests SCAP's response to this apparent copying.

subfiles.title: SCAP response to textile design complaint
subfiles.to: Head of the United Kingdom Liaison Mission, attention Mr. Pierotti
subfiles.about: Reports inquiry into Kanegafuchi's reproduction of Tootal's design.
subfiles.summary: SCAP expects no further orders for the pattern and recommends British design registration in Japan.
